column37: The rule binds electric utilities, municipally owned utilities and electric cooperatives interconnecting large loads to the ERCOT system (subsection (a)); a municipally owned utility or cooperative may add its own requirements: 'Nothing in this section limits the authority of a municipally owned utility or an electric cooperative to impose electric service requirements for large load customers on their systems in addition to the standards adopted under this section' (page 25). Also in the rule, not entered as fields: required disclosures under both agreements (site control with a lease of at least five years, substantially similar requests elsewhere in Texas, water, backup generation, power supply, controllable load resource), audit and verification by ERCOT and commission staff with forfeiture and reallocation for false information (subsections (j), (k)), and the transition for customers that signed a §25.370(g) agreement (subsection (i)). A batch zero load with an interconnection agreement signed on or before 1 June 2025 pays direct interconnection costs under that agreement (subsection (h)(3)(B), page 65). The Texas Register's own pages were not read (sos.state.tx.us answered 403 on the October 9 issue; the adoption was submitted for the issue of 2 October 2026).

column37: A statewide rule binding each New Jersey electric public utility's future large data center tariff (the Maryland and Pennsylvania model rows are alike). The enacted text is Section 1 as numbered 31 in the Fourth Reprint; the bracketed, deleted Section 1 of earlier reprints (100 MW, 85 percent for not less than 10 years) is not the law and is not quoted. Existing service: a large data center approved by a utility before the act's effective date is exempt from paragraphs (1), (2) and (8) of subsection d (the 85 percent guarantee, the security, the study costs) for the approved megawatts only (Section 1g). Other required tariff terms: demand flexibility commitments, priority curtailment before residential customers in system emergencies, disclosure of similar requests pending at other utilities (Section 1b(11) and (12), 1d(5)).
